angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 500,208 km at 197.79 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.0558 +/- 0.0124 mas (same row, RUWE 0.98): 197.79 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.719 +/- 0.013 solar radii from Martioli et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-3568 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...690A.312M/abstract): 500,208 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.78 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Martioli et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-3568 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...690A.312M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4969 +/- 45 K from Martioli et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-3568 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...690A.312M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Martioli et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-3568 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...690A.312M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-3568.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.617, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
